children: AirBaltic's board says the carrier had been facing “acute financial stress” because of a combination of financial and geopolitical factors
Latvia's flag carrier airBaltic has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York, seeking to restructure its debt as the Iran war intensifies pressure on the global airline industry.

The airline said it has secured commitments for €350 million ($405 million) in debtor-in-possession financing from lenders including Strategic Value Partners, Barclays, Hayfin Capital Management, Morgan Stanley and Oaktree Capital Management. The funding is intended to support operations during the court-supervised restructuring.

AirBaltic's board said the carrier had been facing “acute financial stress” because of a combination of financial and geopolitical factors. The airline had been negotiating with creditors for additional short-term funding, but growing concerns over its ability to meet its obligations pushed bond yields sharply higher.

The Chapter 11 filing is aimed at giving airBaltic protection from creditors while it works on a broader restructuring of its balance sheet. The airline said flights would continue as scheduled during the process, with existing tickets and reservations remaining valid.
The carrier expects to complete the restructuring by June 2027. It is majority-owned by the Latvian government, while Lufthansa holds a minority stake.

The filing comes as airlines face a sharp deterioration in operating conditions following the escalation of the Iran conflict. Higher oil prices have pushed up jet fuel costs, adding pressure on carriers that entered the crisis with already stretched balance sheets.

AirBaltic had also been seeking approval from bondholders for up to €257 million of new super-senior debt, with the proposed financing carrying a 25 per cent interest rate. The new debt would have ranked ahead of the airline's existing bonds.
The airline's Chapter 11 filing makes it the second carrier to enter bankruptcy proceedings amid the conflict, following Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy in May.
